items.evidence: After `page.reload()` the spec asserts the note text is visible exactly once (order-note.spec.ts, diff lines 84-88). Without a saved note this would fail. The sidebar check (lines 72-74) also fails for a superuser session.

Every criterion has an assertion: the actor is `test.use({ actor: "order" })` plus the Catalog-hidden/Order-drafts-visible sidebar check, the note is asserted in the history after adding, and again after the reload.
It extends the existing `OrderPage` and reuses `statusInfo`, `goto`, `findOrderId` and `ORDERS_SCENARIO`. `e2e/pages/` has no note or sidebar-menu locators yet, so nothing is duplicated.
There is no waitForTimeout, sleep or polling loop. The waits are on the note locator and on `statusInfo`.
`test`/`expect` come from `../../fixtures/test.ts`. There is no `parallel()` tag and nothing writes to the cache or the dumps.

No test ids exist for the note form, so it uses role-and-name locators (textbox "Comment", button "Add Comment") and sidebar test ids. The note is found by its exact, unique text. There are no CSS, XPath or positional selectors.
It uses the scenario's existing unpaid order through `findOrderId`. The note is the action under test, not set-up.
There are no hard-coded ids and no populatedb names, numbers or prices. The note text comes from the test itself and the author's name is not asserted.
It runs as the single-permission `order` actor through `test.use`. There is no UI login and no credentials.
typecheck.txt reports `exit 0: no errors`, and the spec is at e2e/tests/orders/order-note.spec.ts.
All the new locators and the `addNote` action are on `OrderPage`. The spec only calls page-object members.
The new members are `readonly` fields initialised from `this.page`, and the existing `constructor(readonly page: Page) {}` is kept.
It has `// Arrange` and `// Act & Assert` comments (diff lines 63, 69).
It is one test with a `test.step` for each stage: the permission check, adding the note, and the reload.
The title "Order staff can leave a note that stays in the order history #e2e" describes the behaviour and carries the tag.
The header comment says what the spec covers and why the permission check is there (diff lines 52-57).
All assertions are web-first (`toBeVisible`, `toBeHidden`, `toHaveValue`, `toHaveCount`).
It uses `ORDERS_SCENARIO` and `findOrderId(config, "unpaid")`. The note text is the test's own input, not a scenario value, and no money is compared.
There is no cleanup, and the note text is fixed rather than unique or timestamped.
There are no per-test timeouts, retries, `networkidle` or `waitForLoadState`. After the reload it waits on `statusInfo`, as `goto` does.
The relative imports keep `.ts`, and nothing comes from `@playwright/test` in the spec.
There is no `any`, no cast and no raw gql call.
The comments explain why: the Catalog item proves the session is not a superuser, the positive control, why the reload proves persistence, and why `addNote` waits on the rendered note.

Running as the `order` actor, the spec checks the session in the sidebar (Catalog hidden, Order drafts visible), adds a note through new `OrderPage` members and confirms the note is shown exactly once after a reload. That last check would fail if the save never happened. Nothing duplicates an existing helper, the selectors are role- and test-id-based, and the type check passes (exit 0). The diff also adds a planning note at specs/order-note.md; it isn't a test, so no item covers it.
